summary.prose: Complete the approved activation-blocking bugfix by making native qualification both meaningful and reachable. ac1: the restricted launch disables unwanted plugins, hooks, inherited instructions and auto-memory while retaining OAuth and the scoped bridge. ac2: versioned evidence distinguishes the schema-output protocol tool from executable capabilities and independently reconstructs every required result; unknown or contradictory facts refuse. ac3: the real installed runner emits a completed candidate only after both modes prove the capability boundary, ordered ACKs and actual teardown. ac4: unchanged readiness/evaluation/reconciliation gates lead to a real new-engine review and explicit activation handoff; diagnostics alone cannot complete this fix. The boundary concerns review-agent capabilities/customization, not OS isolation of the CLI or its necessary authentication/network transport.

dataModelChanges.details: Claude v2 evidence explicitly declares boundary review-agent-capabilities-v1. Preserve version1 envelope for compatibility; add optional typed boundary/protocolTools/evidenceBasis fields required only for Claude v2. builtinTools continues to enumerate executable tools and must be empty; protocolTools explicitly records StructuredOutput with schema/launch binding. Existing v1 scripted/native schemas retain their old rules and cannot mint v2 evidence. Each of the 14 required checks has one bounded basis record referencing same-attempt raw evidence digests and policy version; no unknown basis. Denials describe agent exposures; CLI OAuth/transport is outside them. Source inventory distinguishes excluded user/project/local from managed inputs; unmanaged exclusion requires actual bound host policy and active native controls, not absent output alone. Managed inputs require native policy provenance or refuse. Exact additive effective fields: boundary?: 'review-agent-capabilities-v1'; protocolTools?: readonly {name:'StructuredOutput';schemaDigest:string}[]; evidenceBasis?: readonly {check:required-check;basis:'native-catalog'|'native-source-policy-control'|'native-permission-broker'|'host-cross-run'|'durable-journal'|'actual-process-exit';policyVersion:1;rawDigests:readonly string[]}[]. V2 requires boundary plus complete unique basis entries, exact protocol tool/schema digest and 64hex raw digests. V1 rejects v2 fields; v2 identity+source pin distinguishes policy interpretation. Collector alone cannot create these fields. Candidate construction occurs only after verified basis replay. Native diagnostic grammar must be demonstrated against installed CLI before implementation is considered feasible; no invented native source-completeness assertion. Installed feasibility evidence now exists: /tmp/insrc-qualification-feasibility-LlcutM/native-debug.log from one synthetic CliProvider.completeStructured call on Claude2.1.310. Recognized native diagnostics report Found4 plugins(0enabled,4disabled), Registered0hooks from0plugins, Initialized versioned plugins system with0plugins, and cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin not seated:no managed settings and not a Team or Enterprise organization(max). Parser must bind those exact-version messages to the same actual native invocation; host must additionally verify the named managed-settings path is absent (not broken symlink) and no later conflicting managed/plugin/hook/instruction events. Do not assume that the existing debug wording proves arbitrary future organization/remote policy state. The actual schema-only dispatch finished successfully with the disabled-plugin policy. Raw diagnostic/file bytes remain private, bounded and hashed; redact before any user-facing report. No full live qualification is claimed by this feasibility test.

One export owns exactly one attempt identity and ordered control/restricted pair; it owns zero-or-one candidate, exactly one candidate when completed. Add bounded native diagnostic/source-policy evidence kind if needed; same private fixture root, no links, file hashes and combined retention. Qualification facts are host reconstructed: tools/network/shell/raw-filesystem from exact native available-tool/MCP inventory; plugins/hooks/instructions from explicit disabling policy, complete native applicable inventory/source diagnostics and active labelled controls; user/project MCP from exact connected dynamic-only server inventory and strict config; approval from native permission mode/template plus host broker refusal; cross-run from six real foreign-field refusals between positive reads; progress/cancel from durable journal and actual process observation. A control hit never by itself proves restricted denial. Raw canary status remains honestly unverifiable on silence; host combined basis explains why the resulting policy-scoped denial is justified. Relationship directions: export->phases 1:2 ordered owned; export->raw 1:many owned; export->candidate 1:0..1 derived; approved probe record->candidate 1:1 referenced; readiness->mode probes 1:2 referenced, never owns their approval.

Reuse canonical mode-specific probe ISSUE, independent oracle/evaluation ISSUE, readiness ISSUE, predecessor reconciliation AMD and installed authority. Do not add signatures or delete gates. Inventory existing pending records first; prepare exact missing documents/pins and present for explicit approval as needed. Build acceptance requires genuine installed completed candidates for both source modes and a real explicitly scoped plan-investigation-v1 review after its prerequisites are approved. If prerequisite approval is pending, mark acceptance pending and name it; do not claim completion or reroute to legacy. Final default activation signoff and subsequent legacy CODE deletion remain separate human decisions.

errorCases.scenario: Unknown or executable tool/plugin appears in restricted native inventory
errorCases.detection: Exact native mode catalog/protocol allowlist, plugin list and permission-mode checks detect extra, missing or duplicate fields/names.
errorCases.response: Fail attempt; preserve bounded raw output and offending check; no candidate, retry or activation.

errorCases.scenario: Missing policy-source provenance or managed customization overrides restrictions
errorCases.detection: Versioned native diagnostics/source inventory cannot establish exclusions or reports active managed hooks/instructions/plugins.
errorCases.response: Unsupported with exact missing source/check; do not fabricate empty effective arrays or mark build complete. Resolve supported diagnostics or explicitly revise design rather than waive.
errorCases.userImpact: Precise incompatibility surfaced for correction; no false qualification.

errorCases.scenario: Control inactive, native stream malformed, hidden capability or model assertion used as proof
errorCases.detection: Control markers and native inventory completeness fail; independent replay rejects model result fields, duplicate init/version conflicts and contradictory evidence.
errorCases.response: No candidate; failure for actual leak, unsupported for missing evidence.

errorCases.scenario: Tampered/stale/foreign raw evidence, launch or candidate
errorCases.detection: Private real paths, file ownership/modes/hashes, same-attempt bindings and deterministic candidate reconstruction mismatch; current source/binary/profile/catalog/config pins differ.
errorCases.userImpact: Requires deliberate fresh verification; no automatic model rerun.

errorCases.scenario: Budget/deadline/capture overflow, operator cancel or daemon crash
errorCases.detection: Existing aggregate128K/300sec/8MiB admission, cancellation signal, process observer and persisted attempt status.
errorCases.response: Await actual drain, retain diagnostics/checkpoints; operator cancel/interruption never becomes completed. Resume/status same identity without automatic replay.
errorCases.userImpact: Bounded work and honest incomplete acceptance.

errorCases.scenario: Qualification passed but readiness/evaluation/reconciliation approval absent
errorCases.detection: Existing adoption policy reads current canonical approved references/source/profile/catalog/policy pins.
errorCases.response: Prepare/present concrete missing records and retain pending real-review acceptance; no legacy substitution or default flip.
errorCases.userImpact: Human approval of known evidence is the remaining step, not an unexplained blocker.

migration.stateBefore: s1 analyzer and direct reads show Claude v1 empty configuration, generic builtin/plugin failure classification, diagnostic-only runner without candidate, and installed export/adoption gates already present. Actual probes on6693bf60f fail, while scripted continuation infrastructure exists; default engine is legacy.
migration.stateAfter: Claude v2 capability-scoped evidence and shared restriction policy can yield an independently replayed completed installed candidate. Source-only and indexed-impact qualification plus existing canonical evaluation/readiness/reconciliation approvals support one explicit real-engine acceptance review. Default switch remains a separate signoff.

migrationSteps.action: Add strict optional v2 evidence fields and current-policy validators while preserving v1 interpretation and default legacy; extend negative and positive fixtures.
Deploy shared restricted configuration and completed candidate construction with installed replay; update daemon only after source/build tests, checking other sessions before restart.
Run one deliberate serial installed control/restricted pair per mode with saved request IDs and pinned source; inspect actual raw proof. Do not automatically retry failed diagnostics.

Prepare concrete mode probe records and independent oracle/evaluation/readiness evidence plus existing predecessor amendment; obtain explicit approvals where required. Pending approvals keep real-review acceptance pending.

With explicit test opt-in and approved pins, enable only the required scheduling selection for one real plan-investigation-v1 acceptance review of relevant committed scope. Preserve prior config and drain/restore on failure. Do not substitute legacy or claim production default activation.
Present successful acceptance and exact activation configuration for final signoff; default activation and legacy CODE deletion require separate subsequent decisions.

migration.backwardCompat: No rewrite of old diagnostics, approved history or saved legacy states. V1 retains existing interpretation; only v2 can carry the new boundary/protocol/basis contract. New strict optional fields require matching updated daemon and adapter; unsupported versions refuse. Codex and design review remain unchanged. Engine rollout preserves status/cancel/accepted receipts and frozen publication.
